session.about: Manage chat sessions: create, send, open, list, get, rename, move, clear project, fork, archive

create.about: Create a new chat session and send a prompt in it (fire-and-forget)
create.afterHelp:
Examples:
  distillctl session create --prompt "Triage the failing nightly build" \
    --harness-id claude-acp --from "the release orchestrator" --json
  distillctl session create --prompt "Plan the migration" \
    --harness-id codex-acp --model-id gpt-5.6-sol --effort xhigh --fast-mode
  distillctl session create --prompt "Implement the fix" \
    --project-id <project-id> --startup-name my-feature

Result:
  {"session_id": "...", "title": "...", "harness_id": "...",
   "model_id": "..."|null, "effort": "..."|null,
   "fast_mode": true|false|null, "send_status": "dispatched",
   "deprecated": "..."?}
  "model_id", "effort" and "fast_mode" echo the choices the session was
  created with; null leaves that choice to the harness or model default.
  "deprecated" appears when --model-id folded an effort in and says what to
  pass instead. The session runs in the background; the user's view does not
  change. Check progress later with
  `distillctl session get --session-id <session_id>`.

send.about: Send a prompt into an existing chat session
send.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl session send --session-id <session-id> \
    --prompt "Check the latest CI failure" --if-running queue \
    --from "the Distill session handling CI" --delivery-id <stable-id> --json

Result:
  {"session_id": "...", "send_status": "dispatched"|"steered"|"queued"|"deduplicated"}
  The user's current view does not change.

open.about: Open a session in the app window the user is looking at
open.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl session open --session-id <session-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the session is now on screen.

list.about: List the user's chat sessions (most recent first)
list.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl session list --query "review" --limit 10 --json

Result:
  {"sessions": [{"session_id": "...", "title": "...",
                 "project_id": "..."|null, "effort": "..."|null,
                 "fast_mode": true|false|null, "updated_at": "...",
                 "is_running": false, "chat_state": "idle",
                 "message_count": 12}, ...]}
  Most recent first; archived sessions are excluded. "effort" and
  "fast_mode" are what each session's model last acknowledged; null means
  none was recorded and the model runs at its own default.

get.about: Read one session's metadata and optionally its latest messages
get.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl session get --session-id <session-id> --messages 5 --json

Result:
  {"session_id": "...", "title": "...", "harness_id": "...",
   "model_id": "..."|null, "effort": "..."|null,
   "fast_mode": true|false|null, "agent_id": "..."|null,
   "project_id": "..."|null, "working_dir": "..."|null,
   "created_at": "...", "updated_at": "...", "archived": false,
   "is_running": false, "is_open_in_window": false,
   "chat_state": "idle", "message_count": 12,
   "messages": [{"role": "user"|"assistant"|null, "text": "..."}, ...]}
  "effort" and "fast_mode" are the reasoning effort and fast mode the
  session's model last acknowledged, in the harness's own words; null means
  none was recorded and the model runs at its own default. "messages" is
  present only when --messages > 0; each message text is truncated to 2000
  chars.

rename.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl session rename --session-id <session-id> --title "CI triage"

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the new title appears immediately in the app's session list.

move.about: Move a chat session into a project
move.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl session move --session-id <session-id> --project-id <project-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the app's session list regroups immediately.

clear-project.about: Move a chat session out of any project
clear-project.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl session clear-project --session-id <session-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the app's session list regroups immediately.

fork.about: Fork a chat session into an independent copy with its history
fork.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl session fork --session-id <session-id> --title "Alternate approach"

Result:
  {"session_id": "...", "title": "...", "source_session_id": "...",
   "harness_id": "...", "model_id": "..."|null, "effort": "..."|null,
   "fast_mode": true|false|null, "message_count": 7}
  The fork appears in the session list with a copy of the original history.
  "harness_id", "model_id", "effort" and "fast_mode" are what the fork's model
  acknowledged when it opened; null means the model's own default.

archive.about: Archive a chat and clean up its Distill-managed Git resources
archive.afterHelp:
The command refuses to archive when Git cleanup would discard local files or changes,
and distillctl cannot override that: only the user can confirm the loss, in the app.
It also refuses while the chat still has running terminals: archiving in the app
stops that chat's shells, and distillctl will not end a dev server, a build or a
migration on its own. --discard-changes is accepted for compatibility and
has no effect. The command never opens an interactive prompt.

Example:
  distillctl session archive --session-id <session-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the session was archived and eligible worktrees and branches were removed.

folder.about: Manage attached chat folders: attach, detach, replace, set cwd, list

attach.about: Attach a folder, repository, or worktree to a chat
attach.afterHelp:
Use this after creating or adopting a folder inside a workspace root already authorized for the chat. Registered Git worktrees of an authorized repository are also allowed; select a new unrelated root in Distill first.

Example:
  distillctl folder attach --session-id <session-id> --path ~/src/repo-worktrees/feature

Result:
  {"ok": true, "path": "...", "kind": "...", "branch": "..."|null}

detach.about: Detach a folder, repository, or worktree from a chat
detach.afterHelp:
Detach the checked-out folder to detach its branch from chat context. This does not delete anything from disk or Git.

Example:
  distillctl folder detach --session-id <session-id> --path ~/src/repo-worktrees/feature

Result:
  {"ok": true, "path": "...", "detached": true|false}

replace.about: Replace the chat's current folder with another
replace.afterHelp:
Prefer this over set-cwd when the user says to switch or move the chat to a new worktree/folder and does not ask to retain the old folder as context. Use set-cwd to select an already attached folder or when the old attachment should remain.

The old path must be attached. For the usual switch flow, get the current cwd from `distillctl folder list` and pass it as --old-path.

Example:
  distillctl folder replace --session-id <session-id> --old-path ~/src/repo --new-path ~/src/repo-worktrees/feature

Result:
  {"ok": true, "oldPath": "...", "newPath": "...", "kind": "...", "branch": "..."|null}

set-cwd.about: Select a chat folder as cwd, retaining other attachments
set-cwd.afterHelp:
For a request to switch or move the chat to a new worktree/folder, prefer `folder replace` so the old folder leaves context. Use this command when selecting among attachments or intentionally retaining the old folder.

The path must satisfy the same authorization rules as folder attach. Files and Git state are not moved.

Example:
  distillctl folder set-cwd --session-id <session-id> --path ~/src/repo-worktrees/feature

Result:
  {"ok": true, "path": "...", "kind": "...", "branch": "..."|null, "status": "applied"|"pending"}

list.about: List folders attached to a chat and identify its cwd
list.afterHelp:
The top-level cwd is returned even when it is Distill's implicit default and is not an attached folder.

Example:
  distillctl folder list --session-id <session-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true, "cwd": "...", "folders": [{"path": "...", "kind": "...", "branch": "..."|null, "cwd": true|false}]}

project.about: Manage projects: create, list, get, set startup mode, archive

create.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl project create --name "Code reviews" \
    --instructions "Prefer small diffs" \
    --working-dir /Users/me/src/api --working-dir /Users/me/src/web

Result:
  {"project_id": "..."} — the project appears immediately in the app's
  project list with both directories attached.

set-startup-mode.about: Set how a project's new chats start from its Git workspaces

archive.about: Archive a project (reversible; nothing is deleted)
archive.afterHelp:
Archiving is reversible from the app's archive view; nothing is
deleted, and the project's sessions are left untouched.

Example:
  distillctl project archive --project-id <project-id>

Result:
  {"ok": true} — the project disappears from the app's project list.

create.afterHelp:
Examples:
  distillctl agent create --name "Reviewer" \
    --system-prompt "You review diffs for correctness; be terse."
  distillctl agent create --name "Planner" --system-prompt "You plan migrations." \
    --provider codex-acp --model gpt-5.6-sol --effort xhigh --fast-mode

Result:
  {"agent_id": "...", "deprecated": "..."?} — the agent is saved and
  becomes available in future chats; pass it as --agent-id to
  `distillctl session create`. Its chats start on the saved model, effort
  and fast mode. "deprecated" appears when --model folded an effort in
  and says what to pass instead.

list.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl agent list --json

Result:
  {"agents": [{"agent_id": "...", "name": "...",
               "summary": "...", "builtin": false}, ...]}
  Use an agent_id as --agent-id when creating a session.

create.about: Create a new skill (saved as a SKILL.md)
create.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl skill create --name "release-notes" \
    --description "Draft release notes from merged PRs" \
    --content "$(cat SKILL.md)"

Result:
  {"skill_id": "..."} — the skill is saved as a SKILL.md and auto-loads
  into future sessions.

list.about: List the user's skills (name and description only)
list.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl skill list --json

Result:
  {"skills": [{"skill_id": "...", "name": "...",
               "description": "...",
               "source": "app"|"builtin"|"global"|"project"}, ...]}
  Read a skill's full content with `distillctl skill get`.

get.about: Read one skill including its SKILL.md instructions

info.about: Look up installed harnesses, available models, and the app context

harnesses.about: List the agent harnesses sessions can run on, with readiness
harnesses.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl info harnesses --json

Result:
  {"harnesses": [{"harness_id": "claude-acp", "name": "...",
                  "is_default": true,
                  "status": "ready"|"not_installed"|"not_ready"}, ...]}
  Only "ready" harnesses accept new sessions; "not_installed" and
  "not_ready" (sign-in or setup required) need the user to fix them in
  the app first.

models.about: List the models available per agent harness
models.afterHelp:
Example:
  distillctl info models --harness-id codex-acp --json

Result:
  {"harnesses": [{"harness_id": "...",
                  "models": [{"model_id": "...", "name": "...",
                              "provider": "..."?,
                              "group": "main"|"more",
                              "efforts": ["low", "high", ...]|null,
                              "default_effort": "..."|null,
                              "supports_fast": true|false|null}],
                  "warning": "..."?}]}
  Model, effort and fast mode are separate choices: a model_id never carries
  an effort. Pass a model_id (with its harness) as --model-id when creating a
  session, pick --effort from that model's "efforts", and pass --fast-mode
  only where "supports_fast" is true. "efforts": [] means the model has no
  effort control; null in "efforts" or "supports_fast" means the app has not
  learned what the model offers. "group" is the picker page the model is
  filed under ("more" is the More models page). "warning" appears when a
  stale cached list was served or when the harness manages its model outside
  the app.

context.about: Read what the user is looking at in the app right now
